claims: A 2026 class-action lawsuit titled Russell George v. Costco was filed against Costco.
The lawsuit was filed by California resident Russell George.
The lawsuit was filed in early April 2026.
The lawsuit alleges that Costco violates California's Automatic Renewal Law (ARL) by sending membership renewal notices 60 days in advance.
California's Automatic Renewal Law (ARL) requires sending membership renewal notices within a 15 to 45-day window.
The lawsuit claims that sending membership renewal notices 60 days in advance prevented customers from easily canceling.
The lawsuit seeks a jury trial.
The lawsuit argues that sending notice 60 days before charging the card is too early.
The lawsuit argues that sending notice 60 days before charging the card fails to give consumers proper notice to cancel.
The complaint alleges violations of California's False Advertising Law.
The complaint alleges violations of Unfair Competition Law.
The complaint alleges violations of Consumers Legal Remedies Act.
The lawsuit claims that the early notice resulted in automatic charges of $65 for renewals the user did not want.
A preliminary hearing for the case is slated for June 2026.
